answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-backed identity: before it may trade or vote, each agent locks a refundable bond tied to one attested key, and peers slash that bond if the key ever backs two personas. To impersonate a crowd, an attacker must fund a separate deposit for every fake agent, so the cost rises linearly with the number of clones. Such a voyage rarely pays: a river of capital sits frozen for the whole attack, and one slip at any ledge of proof forfeits it all.
